figures.caption: Figure 3: Architecture of the two-stage retrieval framework. Stage 1 utilizes a Transformer-based encoder to process raw tabular features into dense sheet tokens. Stage 2 uses a graph retriever to connect candidate sheets, refine their relationships, and output the final retrieved sheets.

Figure 1: Overview of the Sheet as Token framework. Raw workbook sheets are first converted into schema-aware records, encoded into dense Sheet Tokens, and then processed by a query-specific Graph Retriever to identify supporting sheet sets.

Figure 5: Data preparation pipeline. Real-world and synthetically generated tables are processed into three JSON artifacts (sheets.json, train.json, query.json) that supply pairwise and listwise supervision to the two trained components. Color coding: yellow = inputs, blue = released supervision, green = trained models. Section B details the Valentine-based pair generation procedure.

Table 2: Per-category breakdown of the corpus. Some raw categories (Engineering Quotes, Weibo Comments, Government Projects, Stock Forum Sentiment) were dropped during preprocessing due to empty headers, non-UTF-8 encodings, or row counts exceeding the fabricator’s input limit; these are documented in the release notes but do not contribute sheets.

Figure 4: Training dynamics of the full two-stage retrieval pipeline. The left plot shows accuracy, and the right plot shows normalized entropy. In each plot, the curves correspond to Stage 1 Sheet Token Encoder training and evaluation, and Stage 2 Graph Retriever training and evaluation.

Figure 2: Transformation of a raw spreadsheet into a schema-aware semantic record. The feature extractor maps the sheet’s name, grid dimensions, column headers, and a value example into a structured JSON format, isolating structural semantics while discarding redundant row-level content.
